So, if he tells his co-worker that he was the only one promoted, what does that say about him? On one hand, sharing news about a promotion could be seen as a way to celebrate his achievement. It's natural to want to share good news with colleagues. However, the way he presents it might be problematic. By saying he was the only one promoted, he could be implying that he's better than his co-worker or that his co-worker didn't deserve a promotion. That might come off as boastful or even arrogant. Especially if Jack is already seen as undependable, this kind of statement could reinforce a negative perception. It might make his co-worker feel bad or undervalued, which isn't a good way to maintain positive workplace relationships. On the other hand, maybe Jack is just proud of his achievement and didn't intend to make his co-worker feel bad. Sometimes people share news without considering how it might affect others. But in this case, the way he phrased it could be interpreted negatively. I also wonder about the workplace culture. In some environments, celebrating individual achievements is encouraged, while in others, teamwork and modesty are valued more. If the workplace values humility, then Jack's statement might be seen as inappropriate. Another angle is the potential impact on team dynamics. If Jack is the only one promoted, it could create tension or competition among colleagues. This might lead to a less collaborative environment, which isn't beneficial for the team or the organization. Considering Jack's dependability, if he's known to be undependable, his co-workers might already have reservations about him. It might negatively impact his relationships with his co-workers and the overall team dynamics.
